parsed.explanation: The combined regime layers a national binary passport/visa policy, refusal and possible lifetime fraud-ineligibility risk, and documented immigration-custody abuse over state and municipal facility bans. In the division, a recent mob attack over restroom use ended with the trans victims charged, no attacker arrested that day, one victim denied hospital care and placed in a men's jail and searched by a male guard despite a female licence marker. National hate-crime and employment protections exist but are not shown operating for visitors; local public-accommodation and gender-identity hate-crime protections are absent. A lone adult faces border, restroom and police exposure; a family with a trans minor adds care-ban and school-transition threat framing. This is high risk, above imprisonment/execution regimes but below no-detention border-denial anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary sex-marker regime; X marker stopped for new issues; discrepancy or reasonable doubt can trigger refusal, a case-note tag, and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; reports of passports confiscated or blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements; litigation and a legal-aid FAQ challenge or explain the policy.
entry_documents.interaction: A passport check can escalate from secondary screening to refusal or immigration custody; foreign advisories and reported detentions show border-stage risk.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse; corrections practices include hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; division records men's jail and male search despite a female licence marker.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute exists, but no custody protocol protecting trans visitors is documented; the prison LGBTQ order was rescinded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for restroom trespass or disturbing the peace can move into birth-sex custody and invasive search.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Many state/province facility bans; four make certain trans restroom use criminal trespass; the division municipality enacted a severe restroom ordinance and a trans couple was attacked over restroom use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some states/provinces have no mapped ban; the division statewide facilities position is not established; trespass requires willful entry and refusal to depart, not automatic arrest.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local ordinance and police enforcement determine whether facility use becomes confrontation, charge or custody.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors; national orders stigmatize such care; a trans attack victim was denied hospital care; custody reports include denial or removal of hormones.
care_services.protection: Court injunctions block some national orders; no visitor-facing care protection is documented in the division.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or medication need can expose trans status and lead to denial or custody-linked care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; the school-transition order threatens prosecution; local police charged trans victims rather than attackers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states counterterrorism will not target mere disagreement; national hate-crime law covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat rhetoric and local charging decisions can make police a source of risk after outing.

minors_guardians.exposure: The division bans minors' gender-affirming care; national order threatens prosecution of teachers who use preferred names or pronouns or facilitate social transition; restroom enforcement affects families.
minors_guardians.protection: Some national orders are enjoined; no documented visitor-specific protection for trans minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor increases outing points at borders, facilities and any medical encounter.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: August 2026 mob beat a trans couple over restroom use; both victims were charged with disturbing the peace, no attacker was arrested that day; one was denied hospital care and jailed in a men's facility; the homicide figure is an undercount floor and unusable as a rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute exists; the division hate-crime law omits gender identity; no documented prosecution of attackers.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response can convert victimhood into criminal exposure and birth-sex custody.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The division lacks public-accommodation and gender-identity employment protections; its equality index is lowest; local hate-crime law excludes gender identity; the state restroom position is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National hate-crime and employment protections exist; two municipalities ban gender-identity discrimination; a legal-aid FAQ and pending litigation exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: National recourse may exist but is not shown operating for visitors; local remedies are thin.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A has border flagging leading to multi-year imprisonment and possible capital sentence. This dossier has no general trans imprisonment or execution penalty; its harms are refusal, facilities and custody abuse, and local violence. It is therefore above 0.15-A but still high risk.

0.25-B has coercive two-day detention, mockery, extortion and an uncertain warrant without protection. This dossier shares coercive custody and hostile local response, adds national document and refusal machinery plus a documented men's-facility search, but has partial national hate-crime recourse. Similar, slightly riskier than 0.25-B.

0.35-C has an explicit bar on detention for marker discrepancy and only administrative denial of entry. This dossier lacks that bar, documents actual custody harm and a violent confrontation with victims charged, so it is materially below 0.35-C.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a national border and document system that can refuse or permanently bar a trans visitor, layered over state and municipal facility bans and a division where police charged restroom-attack victims, denied hospital care and placed one in a men's jail searched by a male guard. National hate-crime and employment protections are real but not shown to protect visitors, and immigration and correctional custody carry severe documented abuse. A lone adult faces border, restroom and police exposure; a family with a trans minor adds care-ban and school-transition threat framing. The result is high risk, not the catastrophic imprisonment or execution tier.
